facts.label: Analysis: leverage and cover
facts.text: Reported leverage is lower mainly because debt fell, not because earnings rose. The carrying value of total debt dropped from USD 912.145 million at the end of 2025 to USD 624.743 million at 30 September 2026, as proceeds of the 2026 stock offering by the subsidiary ARKO Petroleum Corp. repaid part of the Capital One line and the company bought back USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes for about USD 91.858 million. Over the same window last-twelve-months reported EBITDA slipped to USD 227.442 million from USD 236.861 million, because a gain of about USD 20.8 million on a 2025 sale-leaseback leaves the twelve-month window, so the move in debt to EBITDA from 3.85x to 2.75x is a debt-reduction effect. Basis: calculation C68; calculation C69; calculation C67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76

facts.label: Analysis: cash flow and free cash flow
facts.text: Free cash flow after capital spending was close to zero over the last twelve months: operating cash flow of USD 135.334 million less purchases of property and equipment of USD 134.590 million leaves USD 0.744 million, against USD 65.299 million in 2025 and USD 107.944 million in 2024. The fall is sharpest in the 2026 nine months, when operating cash flow of USD 90.758 million, against USD 148.009 million a year earlier, did not cover purchases of property and equipment of USD 104.945 million, with trade receivables up USD 101.894 million and inventory up USD 31.938 million, partly offset by payables up USD 56.209 million. The filing attributes the decline to higher fuel prices, the day of the week on which the quarter ended and about USD 14.9 million lower dealer deposits received. Part of this is working capital that can reverse, but the company also paid dividends of USD 10.096 million on common stock, USD 4.301 million on preferred stock and USD 9.553 million to outside holders of the subsidiary in the nine months. facts.label: Analysis: liquidity and refinancing
facts.text: The maturity wall is less certain. The only printed schedule, at the end of 2025, places USD 395.694 million in 2028, which is the Capital One line maturing on 2028-05-05, and USD 453.298 million in 2029, which is the Senior Notes due 2029-11-15. Since then the company repaid USD 206.7 million of the Capital One line, repurchased USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes and refinanced its M&T term loans to 2031, so both amounts are now lower, but no updated schedule is printed. The PNC lines mature on the earliest of 2031-02-13 and six months before the Capital One line or the Senior Notes mature, subject to conditions the filing mentions, which on the printed dates is 2027-11-05, so a Capital One extension is needed to keep PNC access beyond 2027. Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The maturity schedule is printed only at 31 December 2025 and the third-quarter report prints none, so the maturity wall after the 2026 repayment of USD 206.7 million of the Capital One line, the Senior Notes repurchase of USD 100.0 million and the M&T refinancing is not established; refinancing work can rest only on the old schedule. Severity High. Action: obtain an updated maturity table from a later annual report or a lender presentation. - The gross principal of debt at 30 September 2026 is not printed, so the reconciling items between principal and carrying value are not established for that date; the stated principal amounts are USD 350.0 million of Senior Notes, USD 178.1 million drawn on the Capital One line, M&T term loans of USD 70.2 million and an equipment line of USD 26.2 million, and insurance premium notes are carried at USD 4.604 million with no principal stated. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the debt table with principal at that date. - Borrowing-base availability under the PNC lines is not stated at 30 September 2026, so the undrawn facilities figure of USD 845.200 million treats those lines as available in full less USD 9.0 million of letters of credit, which makes it a ceiling for liquidity. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the PNC availability calculation. - Covenant levels, reported covenant figures and compliance statements after 31 December 2025 are not printed for the PNC availability test, the M&T liquidity and debt service coverage tests or the Capital One leverage and interest coverage tests, so no covenant headroom is stated and none is inferred. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreements and compliance certificates. - The effect of the pending purchase of U.S. Petroleum Partners assets on net debt and leverage is not established because the inventory value at closing and the closing date are not stated; the cash price is about USD 205 million plus inventory. Severity High. Action: obtain closing terms once the purchase completes. - Figures for the Senior Notes guarantor group, for ARKO Petroleum Corp. alone and for the parent alone at 30 September 2026 are not printed, and the parent-only condensed statements exist only at 31 December 2025, so subsidiary-level leverage and the structural position of the Senior Notes are not quantified. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the separate report of the subsidiary and guarantor information. - Adjusted EBITDA and net debt include all of ARKO Petroleum Corp. although outside holders own 26.4% of its economic interests; the outside share of EBITDA is not printed, and only net income attributable to non-controlling interests of USD 7.974 million in nine months 2026 and dividends to them of USD 9.553 million are stated, so no deconsolidated leverage is shown. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's own EBITDA. - Sale-leaseback financial liabilities of USD 126.435 million at 31 December 2025 are carried in other liabilities and are not itemised at 30 September 2026, so whether they should count as debt, and by how much, is not resolved; Series A redeemable preferred stock of USD 100.0 million is also outside total debt. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the other liabilities note for 2026. - Non-controlling interest net income prints a dash for the fiscal years and the 2025 quarter and nine months, and non-controlling interests on the balance sheet print no line at 31 December 2024 and a dash at 31 December 2025; these cells are written as not supplied and not as zero. Severity Low. Action: none needed for credit work if the interest is nil. - Several cash flow lines are printed only in some periods: business and asset acquisitions in the annual statements only, and the repurchase of long-term debt, the subsidiary offering proceeds and costs and dividends to outside holders in 2026 only; the other columns are written as not supplied. The cash flow table also shows the lines needed for debt, dividends and capital spending and leaves other operating lines inside the printed totals. Severity Low. Action: none. - Several instrument terms are not stated: the principal and amortisation of the M&T loans and the insurance premium notes, the security and rate of the insurance premium notes, and the relative rank of the secured facilities against each other. Insurance premium notes are left out of the debt stack for that reason. Severity Low. Action: obtain the facility documents. - Leverage and cover are computed for 31 December 2024, 31 December 2025 and 30 September 2026 only; balance sheets at 31 March and 30 June 2026 are tabulated and net debt is shown for them, but last-twelve-months EBITDA at those dates was not built. Severity Low. Action: none unless interim leverage is needed. - In the third-quarter report the segment expense lines for salaries and wages, credit card fees, rent, repairs and other expenses lose their column labels in the prepared text, so they were not extracted; segment revenue and operating income were read from aligned rows. Severity Low. Action: use the segment tables in the management discussion for detail. - Interest expense by instrument is not printed, so interest cover uses the group's cash interest paid and no instrument-level cost of debt is stated. Severity Low. Action: none. - The amount of offering proceeds used to repay the Capital One line differs between the 2025 annual report, about USD 184.0 million, and the 2026 quarterly reports, USD 206.7 million; both figures are kept and the later one is used for 2026 facts. Severity Low. Action: none. - The segment operating income of corporate and eliminations is a calculated residual, not a printed line, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is calculated as the fiscal year less nine months because no separate fourth quarter is reported. Severity Low. Action: none.

rows.label: T2D.9 — Sponsor and governance risk assessment — paragraph 1
T2D.9 — Sponsor and governance risk assessment — paragraph 2

limitations: Produced in a host session and accepted by the CP-OS check.
Literal checked analytical handoff, not native contract acceptance; source qualifications and gaps remain.

- The holders of about 59% of the voting stock are not named and no fund life, pledge or exit intention is stated, because the proxy statement that carries directors, ownership and related-party detail is not supplied; the medium governance rating rests on structure and observed actions. Severity High. Action: obtain the proxy statement. - Whether ARKO Petroleum and its subsidiaries guarantee the Senior Notes is not stated after the listing, so the notes' direct claim on subsidiary cash flow is not established. Severity High. Action: obtain the indenture and any supplemental indenture. - Covenant levels, compliance after 2025-12-31 and the capacity for dividends, investments, liens and debt under the PNC, M&T, Capital One and Senior Notes documents are not stated, so legal capacity for shareholder payouts and acquisitions is not measured. Severity High. Action: obtain the credit agreements, the indenture and compliance certificates. - No amounts are printed for the management services, fuel supply and cost-sharing charges between ARKO and ARKO Petroleum after the listing, so leakage from related-party pricing cannot be sized. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's quarterly report and the proxy statement. - The closing date, funding mix, inventory payment and pro forma EBITDA of the pending U.S. Petroleum Partners purchase are not stated, so its effect on leverage at ARKO Petroleum is not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the closing announcement and the next quarterly report. - ARKO Petroleum's own statements, debt and dividend capacity are not supplied, and the parent-only schedule exists only at 2025-12-31, so the parent's upstream cash at 2026-09-30 is not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's own reports. - In the third-quarter report the segment expense tables lose column alignment in the text as supplied, so only segment revenue and operating income were read from them; segment expenses are not analysed. Severity Low. Action: use the aligned tables in the management discussion if segment costs are needed. - No rating, bond price or loan price is supplied, so no market view of governance risk is stated. Severity Low. Action: obtain rating reports and price sources if wanted.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is lower because debt fell, not because earnings rose, so the improvement is a one-time step. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 2.75x at 2026-09-30 against 3.85x at 2025-12-31, since total debt fell 31.51% while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA slipped 3.98%. Net debt to EBITDA is 1.94x, which is 1.95x pro forma for the common dividend payable 2026-12-03 and 1.97x pro forma for the subsidiary dividend payable 2026-11-30, each event taken alone, and the effect of the pending acquisition is not established. Counting finance leases lifts total debt to EBITDA to 3.63x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Free cash flow is the weak link and the main reason the profile is adequate rather than strong. Free cash flow was 47.64% of reported EBITDA in FY2024, 27.57% in FY2025 and 0.33% over the last twelve months, and it was negative in the nine months to 2026-09-30, when operating cash flow fell 38.68% while capital spending rose. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Margins are thin enough that fuel margin decides earnings. Reported EBITDA is 2.74% of revenue over the last twelve months, and a change of one cent per gallon on 2025 volumes moves gross profit by USD 20.64 million, which is 8.71% of 2025 reported EBITDA. Fixed-fee wholesale supply and dealer conversions dampen this, but the company attributes the 2026 rise in fuel margin to fuel-market volatility, which can reverse, and add-backs are 13.94% of Adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is the safer measure. facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Revenue is mostly pass-through fuel, so it is cyclical and price-driven: revenues grew 11.28% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 although fuel gallons fell 7.61%, because the average price of fuel rose, and merchandise revenue fell 12.28% as stores closed or converted and same-store sales declined. Retail fuel margin is the swing factor because retail prices lag wholesale costs; the company says margins are lower when costs rise gradually and higher when costs fall or are volatile. Wholesale and consignment contracts earn a fixed fee or share gross profit, which largely removes exposure to commodity price movements in the wholesale channel. facts.label: Macro, regulatory and political factors
facts.text: Only two groups of factors change the credit conclusion. Economic and political factors matter because fuel prices were volatile in 2026 with the Middle East conflict and supply disruptions, diesel reached record highs in the third quarter, and management says sustained high diesel prices or supply constraints could reduce gallons, compress margins or raise working capital needs, which is the main path from macro conditions to liquidity; 44.0% of debt bore variable rates at 2026-09-30, so a one percentage point rise would add about USD 2.8 million of annual debt service. Regulatory factors matter because cigarette sales explain about 90% of the same-store merchandise decline, tobacco consumption and regulation are named risks, and environmental rules on underground tanks require remediation spending, with environmental capital expenditure of about USD 3.3 million in 2025. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials. Basis: calculation C27; calculation C25; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a sustained spike in wholesale fuel prices, with diesel at record highs as in the third quarter of 2026, together with weaker demand. The first operational break is working capital: receivables and inventory rise as they did in 2026, when three working-capital lines absorbed more cash than the whole fall in operating cash flow, and retail fuel margin is squeezed when costs rise gradually. Operating cash flow then stays below capital spending, so free cash flow turns negative and the payouts to shareholders and the dividends to outside holders of the subsidiary are met from cash balances and revolver borrowing. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C31; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: Financially, borrowing on the Capital One and PNC lines raises debt while EBITDA falls; reported cash interest cover would be 2.0x if EBITDA fell 33.53% at current interest, an illustrative level because no covenant level is printed, and a PNC borrowing base shrinks if receivables and inventory fall. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the 2027 calendar of the Series A redemption right and the PNC maturity of 2027-11-05 arrives with less free cash flow, and the USD 205 million acquisition, if borrowed, would add debt first and earnings later. Management levers are cutting growth capital, stopping buybacks and dividends, slowing conversions and drawing the Capital One line, whose unused amount was USD 621.4 million. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months on stated liquidity, but refinancing risk in 2028 and 2029 would rise sharply. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, ARKO presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a fixed-fee wholesale channel, a fleet fueling base and a repaired balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by thin margins, near-zero free cash flow, secured debt and a minority interest ahead of the unsecured notes, and a crowded funding calendar from late 2027. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because free cash flow conversion fell to 0.33% of EBITDA while 81.21% of retail stores are leased. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the Capital One line before 2027-11-05, on the fuel market, which drives working capital and margin, and on whether the subsidiary's dividends keep reaching the parent. The primary downside path is a fuel price spike that turns working capital into revolver borrowing ahead of the 2027 to 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require covenant levels, a current maturity schedule, the guarantor list and standalone statements for the subsidiary. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing the 2027 to 2029 obligations from thin free cash flow. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; calculation C44; calculation C48

spans.text: # ARKO Corp. — Financial foundation
## Request

Issuer: ARKO Corp., issuer id arko-1823794, as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: statements, net debt, liquidity, maturities and credit metrics from the five supplied filings, with every balance sheet date to 2026-09-30 and last-twelve-months figures to that date. The module draws no recommendation.
## Sources

| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | Source readiness (CP-0) | 4934282bdfbbbc0489c8f0295d56af0d9cb6ce8374b76c0d77feb2eb83b03774 | Source coverage, document dates and limitations of the five filings. |
## Findings
### Bottom line

ARKO's leverage fell to 2.75x debt to reported EBITDA at 30 September 2026 after 2026 stock-offering proceeds repaid bank debt, but interest cover of 3.01x and near-zero free cash flow leave creditors reliant on liquidity and refinancing.
Basis: calculation C27; calculation C29; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21

Net debt to reported EBITDA is 1.94x. On the issuer's adjusted EBITDA the two ratios are 2.36x and 1.67x, but add-backs equal 13.94% of adjusted EBITDA on a last-twelve-months basis. Liquidity is about USD 1.0 billion, but the only maturity table printed predates the 2026 repayments, so the current maturity wall is not established.
Basis: calculation C28; calculation C30; calculation C31; calculation C52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 134
### Analysis: leverage and cover

Reported leverage is lower mainly because debt fell, not because earnings rose. The carrying value of total debt dropped from USD 912.145 million at the end of 2025 to USD 624.743 million at 30 September 2026, as proceeds of the 2026 stock offering by the subsidiary ARKO Petroleum Corp. repaid part of the Capital One line and the company bought back USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes for about USD 91.858 million. Over the same window last-twelve-months reported EBITDA slipped to USD 227.442 million from USD 236.861 million, because a gain of about USD 20.8 million on a 2025 sale-leaseback leaves the twelve-month window, so the move in debt to EBITDA from 3.85x to 2.75x is a debt-reduction effect.
Basis: calculation C68; calculation C69; calculation C67; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 76

Adjusted EBITDA flatters the picture. Add-backs are USD 36.839 million over the twelve months, of which share-based compensation is USD 19.289 million and acquisition, divestiture and disposal items are USD 16.233 million; reported EBITDA, the primary measure here, gives cash interest cover of 3.01x against 3.50x on the adjusted figure. Cover is thin for a business with 44.0% of its debt at variable rates, although a one percentage point rise in rates adds only about USD 2.8 million of annual debt service against USD 75.590 million of cash interest paid over the twelve months.
Basis: calculation C50; calculation C44; calculation C53; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 55–56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64
### Analysis: cash flow and free cash flow

Free cash flow after capital spending was close to zero over the last twelve months: operating cash flow of USD 135.334 million less purchases of property and equipment of USD 134.590 million leaves USD 0.744 million, against USD 65.299 million in 2025 and USD 107.944 million in 2024. The fall is sharpest in the 2026 nine months, when operating cash flow of USD 90.758 million, against USD 148.009 million a year earlier, did not cover purchases of property and equipment of USD 104.945 million, with trade receivables up USD 101.894 million and inventory up USD 31.938 million, partly offset by payables up USD 56.209 million. The filing attributes the decline to higher fuel prices, the day of the week on which the quarter ended and about USD 14.9 million lower dealer deposits received. Part of this is working capital that can reverse, but the company also paid dividends of USD 10.096 million on common stock, USD 4.301 million on preferred stock and USD 9.553 million to outside holders of the subsidiary in the nine months.

Basis: calculation C12; calculation C13; calculation C14; calculation C84; calculation C81; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59
### Analysis: liquidity and refinancing

Liquidity is ample against near-term needs: cash of USD 183.804 million plus undrawn committed facilities of USD 845.200 million, which the company describes as about USD 1.0 billion in total. The undrawn figure takes the PNC lines at their full size less USD 9.0 million of letters of credit, because their borrowing-base availability is not stated at 30 September 2026; those lines depend on receivables and inventory, so this part is a ceiling. The Capital One availability of USD 621.400 million is stated net of USD 178.1 million drawn and USD 0.5 million of letters of credit.

Basis: calculation C37; calculation C38; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 57–58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63

The maturity wall is less certain. The only printed schedule, at the end of 2025, places USD 395.694 million in 2028, which is the Capital One line maturing on 2028-05-05, and USD 453.298 million in 2029, which is the Senior Notes due 2029-11-15. Since then the company repaid USD 206.7 million of the Capital One line, repurchased USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes and refinanced its M&T term loans to 2031, so both amounts are now lower, but no updated schedule is printed. The PNC lines mature on the earliest of 2031-02-13 and six months before the Capital One line or the Senior Notes mature, subject to conditions the filing mentions, which on the printed dates is 2027-11-05, so a Capital One extension is needed to keep PNC access beyond 2027.

### Analysis: perimeter, definitions and data quality

The statements consolidate all of ARKO Petroleum Corp. although the company holds 73.6% of its economic interests, so 26.4% of that subsidiary's earnings and dividends belong to outside holders, while the Capital One line sits at its GPMP subsidiary and the Senior Notes at the parent. Total debt here is the balance-sheet carrying value of the four debt lines and excludes finance lease liabilities of USD 201.436 million, which would lift debt to EBITDA to 3.63x, sale-leaseback financial liabilities of USD 126.435 million at the end of 2025 that are carried in other liabilities, and USD 100.0 million of Series A redeemable preferred stock. Cash excludes USD 12.995 million of restricted cash and USD 8.337 million of short-term investments, while the cash flow statement's closing cash includes restricted cash.
Basis: calculation C70; calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 146–149

A small non-debt funding float also exists: dealer deposits of USD 16.115 million non-current and USD 6.153 million current at the end of 2025, and deferred vendor income of USD 37.026 million non-current and USD 16.475 million current; lower dealer deposits received were one reason nine-month operating cash flow fell. At the parent alone, the 2025 annual report shows cash of USD 2.577 million and loans to subsidiaries of USD 420.0 million against the Senior Notes, so note holders depend on cash moving up from operating subsidiaries, and the Capital One line limits dividends from its borrower to the extent of available cash.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–130; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 159; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 63
### Analysis: subsequent events and multi-figure events

Three events after 30 September 2026 are stated. The pending purchase of U.S. Petroleum Partners assets by the subsidiary is for about USD 205 million of cash plus inventory at closing and USD 30 million of its Class A stock held in escrow, expected to close later in 2026 and to be funded from existing lines of credit; its effect on net debt is not established because the inventory value is not stated, and it is not blended into any period figure. A common dividend of USD 0.03 per share is payable on 2026-12-03 and a subsidiary dividend of USD 0.50 per share on 2026-11-30, together about USD 9.65 million of cash if paid in full, which would add about 0.04x to net leverage; both are shown as pro forma rows only.

| C85 | Finance lease liabilities at 2025-12-31 | Current 13.239 plus non-current 199.691 (US$m) | 212.930 | 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 97 |
## Gaps

- The maturity schedule is printed only at 31 December 2025 and the third-quarter report prints none, so the maturity wall after the 2026 repayment of USD 206.7 million of the Capital One line, the Senior Notes repurchase of USD 100.0 million and the M&T refinancing is not established; refinancing work can rest only on the old schedule. Severity High. Action: obtain an updated maturity table from a later annual report or a lender presentation.

- The gross principal of debt at 30 September 2026 is not printed, so the reconciling items between principal and carrying value are not established for that date; the stated principal amounts are USD 350.0 million of Senior Notes, USD 178.1 million drawn on the Capital One line, M&T term loans of USD 70.2 million and an equipment line of USD 26.2 million, and insurance premium notes are carried at USD 4.604 million with no principal stated. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the debt table with principal at that date.

- Borrowing-base availability under the PNC lines is not stated at 30 September 2026, so the undrawn facilities figure of USD 845.200 million treats those lines as available in full less USD 9.0 million of letters of credit, which makes it a ceiling for liquidity. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the PNC availability calculation.

- Covenant levels, reported covenant figures and compliance statements after 31 December 2025 are not printed for the PNC availability test, the M&T liquidity and debt service coverage tests or the Capital One leverage and interest coverage tests, so no covenant headroom is stated and none is inferred. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the credit agreements and compliance certificates.

- The effect of the pending purchase of U.S. Petroleum Partners assets on net debt and leverage is not established because the inventory value at closing and the closing date are not stated; the cash price is about USD 205 million plus inventory. Severity High. Action: obtain closing terms once the purchase completes.

- Figures for the Senior Notes guarantor group, for ARKO Petroleum Corp. alone and for the parent alone at 30 September 2026 are not printed, and the parent-only condensed statements exist only at 31 December 2025, so subsidiary-level leverage and the structural position of the Senior Notes are not quantified. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the separate report of the subsidiary and guarantor information.

- Adjusted EBITDA and net debt include all of ARKO Petroleum Corp. although outside holders own 26.4% of its economic interests; the outside share of EBITDA is not printed, and only net income attributable to non-controlling interests of USD 7.974 million in nine months 2026 and dividends to them of USD 9.553 million are stated, so no deconsolidated leverage is shown. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's own EBITDA.

- Sale-leaseback financial liabilities of USD 126.435 million at 31 December 2025 are carried in other liabilities and are not itemised at 30 September 2026, so whether they should count as debt, and by how much, is not resolved; Series A redeemable preferred stock of USD 100.0 million is also outside total debt. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the other liabilities note for 2026.

- Non-controlling interest net income prints a dash for the fiscal years and the 2025 quarter and nine months, and non-controlling interests on the balance sheet print no line at 31 December 2024 and a dash at 31 December 2025; these cells are written as not supplied and not as zero. Severity Low. Action: none needed for credit work if the interest is nil.

- Several cash flow lines are printed only in some periods: business and asset acquisitions in the annual statements only, and the repurchase of long-term debt, the subsidiary offering proceeds and costs and dividends to outside holders in 2026 only; the other columns are written as not supplied. The cash flow table also shows the lines needed for debt, dividends and capital spending and leaves other operating lines inside the printed totals. Severity Low. Action: none.

- Several instrument terms are not stated: the principal and amortisation of the M&T loans and the insurance premium notes, the security and rate of the insurance premium notes, and the relative rank of the secured facilities against each other. Insurance premium notes are left out of the debt stack for that reason. Severity Low. Action: obtain the facility documents.

- Leverage and cover are computed for 31 December 2024, 31 December 2025 and 30 September 2026 only; balance sheets at 31 March and 30 June 2026 are tabulated and net debt is shown for them, but last-twelve-months EBITDA at those dates was not built. Severity Low. Action: none unless interim leverage is needed.

- In the third-quarter report the segment expense lines for salaries and wages, credit card fees, rent, repairs and other expenses lose their column labels in the prepared text, so they were not extracted; segment revenue and operating income were read from aligned rows. Severity Low. Action: use the segment tables in the management discussion for detail.
- Interest expense by instrument is not printed, so interest cover uses the group's cash interest paid and no instrument-level cost of debt is stated. Severity Low. Action: none.

- The amount of offering proceeds used to repay the Capital One line differs between the 2025 annual report, about USD 184.0 million, and the 2026 quarterly reports, USD 206.7 million; both figures are kept and the later one is used for 2026 facts. Severity Low. Action: none.

- The segment operating income of corporate and eliminations is a calculated residual, not a printed line, and the fourth quarter of 2025 is calculated as the fiscal year less nine months because no separate fourth quarter is reported. Severity Low. Action: none.

spans.text: # ARKO Corp. — Business & governance
## Request

Issuer: ARKO Corp., issuer id arko-1823794, as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business, ownership, control, governance and shareholder behavior, capital allocation and the 2026 transactions of ARKO Corp., taken from the five supplied SEC filings and the source readiness handoff. No sponsor is named in the filings, and no recommendation or peer comparison is drawn.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2024-12-31_arko_arko-20241231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2024 | 2025-02-26 | 30099d5050db6ac0368f88b28d857a9a9d746a674ed2f8c95454cfa27ad6e5d5 | Business description, store and site counts at 2024-12-31, voting concentration at 2024-12-31, warrants and the start of the Transformation Plan. |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-25 | 21af2950aeb046d875c8fbf588a55748c51fe126978fdd1da364c46cc3697084 | Business and segment description, relationship with ARKO Petroleum, conflict risk factors, voting concentration at 2025-12-31, Series A terms, acquisitions, Blue Owl program, debt note, related parties, share repurchases and parent-only statements. |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_arko_arko-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 | 4fd1f1f4e34e8322139ef7177074fe32c134dcdef8140a6ffe107c26a5fa80fd | Listing of ARKO Petroleum and first-quarter debt repayment and dividends. |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_arko_arko-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-07 | 4cbf20d756410398d38970ce1e4f247d1143b165fdcd63d3abb7dff4057dcd2d | Senior Notes repurchases to 2026-06-30 and the first report of the U.S. Petroleum Partners agreement. |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-05 | 28a3dbf93c9e062092f7330877b3e6a4e6352a114e43313fda25dd33f69ea2c8 | Latest ownership percentages, debt events, pending acquisition, dividends, liquidity, transformation progress and segment results. |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |

| Source readiness | Source readiness (CP-0) | 4934282bdfbbbc0489c8f0295d56af0d9cb6ce8374b76c0d77feb2eb83b03774 | Source status, document dates and what was not supplied (no proxy statement, executed credit documents, ratings or prices). |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Governance risk is medium: no sponsor is named and 2026 actions favored creditors, but the ARKO Petroleum listing and a pending USD 205 million acquisition put more of the cash flow in a partly owned subsidiary. Stock-offering proceeds repaid USD 206.7 million of bank debt and the company repurchased USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes at a discount.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C19

Outside holders own 26.4% of ARKO Petroleum, which earned 48.75% of segment operating income in the nine months to 2026-09-30 and intends to pay USD 2.00 per share a year, about USD 25.14 million of which would go to outside holders. Control sits with a group of unnamed holders, so sponsor intent and exit pressure cannot be assessed.
Basis: calculation C01; calculation C13; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53
### Key findings

Control is concentrated in holders the filings do not name, so there is no sponsor record to underwrite. A limited number of stockholders beneficially owned about 59% of the voting stock at the end of 2025, 8 percentage points less than the 67% a year earlier, but the filings give no names, fund life, board seats or fees because directors, ownership and related-party detail are incorporated by reference from a proxy statement that is not supplied. The Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer holds the same offices at ARKO and its listed subsidiary, so decisions on dividends, related-party terms and acquisitions between the two sit with one management team.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 53; 10-K_2024-12-31_arko_arko-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 42; calculation C37; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 89; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50

The 2026 listing of ARKO Petroleum moved close to half of segment profit into a company that outside holders own 26.4% of, which lowers the share of that cash flow that reaches the parent. ARKO keeps 93.3% of the vote through Class B shares carrying five votes each, so control is not at risk, but ARKO Petroleum intends to pay USD 0.50 per share each quarter, which at that rate sends USD 70.0 million a year to ARKO and USD 25.14 million to outside holders, and its Capital One borrower may pay dividends up the chain only to the extent of available cash. The agreements between ARKO and its subsidiary were prepared when it was wholly owned and were not approved by a separate or disinterested board, and the fixed margin the group sets for its GPMP fuel-supply segment rose from USD 0.05 to USD 0.06 per gallon at the start of 2026.

Basis: calculation C13; calculation C01; calculation C08; calculation C09; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10

Behavior toward creditors has so far been supportive. Total debt fell 31.51% between 2025-12-31 and 2026-09-30 because stock-offering proceeds repaid USD 206.7 million of the Capital One line and the company repurchased USD 100.0 million of Senior Notes at an 8.14% discount. No dividend recapitalization, priming, uptier, drop-down, waiver or default is described in the five filings, and the covenants were reported as met at the end of 2025.

Basis: calculation C18; calculation C19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135

Payouts to shareholders have taken a rising share of free cash flow and in 2026 exceeded it, which is the one behavior that points the other way. Dividends and buybacks equalled 47.95% of free cash flow in FY2024 and 72.49% in FY2025, and in the nine months to 2026-09-30 free cash flow was negative while dividends and buybacks continued. At the parent alone, cash fell USD 22.56 million in 2025 to a small balance after a USD 30.0 million repayment of loans by subsidiaries, so noteholders depend on money moving up from operating subsidiaries.
Basis: calculation C22; calculation C25; calculation C30; calculation C32; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 159–160; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

The USD 100.0 million Series A preferred stock is the one claim that can force a cash call in 2027, and it limits how far leverage can rise. From 2027-08-31 holders of a majority, or the company, can give notice to redeem at the USD 100.0 million liquidation preference, the 5.75% cumulative dividend costs USD 5.75 million a year, and holder consent is needed for new debt that takes leverage above 7.00x on the agreement's own definition, which is not supplied. Conversion at USD 11.46 per share is far from the USD 5.03 per share at which shares were withheld in August 2026, so redemption is the likelier outcome, and the redemption right opens about two months before 2027-11-05, the date on which the PNC lines mature if the Capital One line is not extended.

Basis: calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C42; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 149; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

Acquisition appetite is returning after a pause and is to be funded with debt at ARKO Petroleum. No acquisition closed in 2025 or the nine months of 2026, leaving 26 completed since 2013, but ARKO Petroleum agreed on 2026-08-04 to buy the business of U.S. Petroleum Partners for about USD 205 million in cash plus USD 30 million of its own stock, to be financed under existing lines of credit. Against the USD 31.7 million EBITDA target that sets the earn-out, the USD 235.0 million consideration is 7.41x, an analyst calculation and not reported earnings. Past deals leaned on sale-leasebacks with the real estate investor Blue Owl, which provided 66.92% of the consideration for the 2023 Transit Energy Group acquisition, so growth has added lease and financing liabilities rather than equity.

Basis: calculation C35; calculation C36; calculation C47; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 122–123; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 38

The Transformation Plan is making ARKO more of a fuel distributor, which should steady earnings through fixed-fee fuel supply but leaves less merchandise profit and a lease-heavy site base. The retail store count is 25.27% below its level at the end of 2024 and dealer supply sites are 10.51% higher, management says the conversions have added USD 15.6 million of incremental operating income over twelve months, and the plan is expected to be largely complete by the end of 2027. Against that, merchandise revenue fell 12.28% and fuel gallons 7.61% in the nine months, merchandise margin rose to 34.5% from 33.5%, and 81.21% of retail stores are leased, with lease liabilities at 1.83x total debt at the end of 2025.

Basis: calculation C14; calculation C15; calculation C17; calculation C16; calculation C38; calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139

Public reporting is sound, but creditor-specific governance terms are thin. Internal control over financial reporting was effective at the end of 2025 and audited by an independent registered firm, related-party disclosure was unchanged in the third quarter of 2026 and covenant compliance was reported at the end of 2025; board composition, independence, fees to holders, covenant levels and any compliance statement after 2025-12-31 are not in the filings supplied.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 33; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a medium reading is the repair already made. Total debt is 31.51% lower than at the end of 2025, the Senior Notes were repurchased below par, covenants were reported as met at the end of 2025, no default or waiver is described, the parent still receives 73.6% of ARKO Petroleum's dividends, and the share of voting stock held by the unnamed group fell by 8 percentage points in a year. A proxy statement showing independent directors, a conflicts committee that reviewed the post-listing fuel supply and cost-sharing terms, and no pledge of the large holders' shares would move the view toward low.

Basis: calculation C18; calculation C37; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 135; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 65

Three developments would move the view toward high: the U.S. Petroleum Partners acquisition closing on Capital One borrowings that raise leverage materially, the Series A redemption right being met from revolver borrowing in 2027, or a release of ARKO Petroleum or its subsidiaries from the Senior Notes guarantee together with dividends above USD 2.00 per share a year. A covenant waiver or an amendment on weaker terms would do the same.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147
### Limitations

- The holders of the roughly 59% voting block are not named because the proxy statement is not supplied, so the medium rating rests on structure and observed actions and not on any owner's record; a named sponsor with a fund life or pledged shares would move it either way.

- Whether ARKO Petroleum and its subsidiaries guarantee the Senior Notes is not stated after the listing, so the view that noteholders keep a claim on the subsidiary's cash flow is limited to the dividends and loans that reach the parent.

- The credit agreements, indenture and Series A terms are described but not supplied, so covenant levels, the definition of the 7.00x consent test and restricted-payment capacity are not established, and no conclusion on headroom after 2025-12-31 can be drawn.

- No amounts are printed for the management services, fuel supply or cost-sharing charges between ARKO and ARKO Petroleum after the listing, so any leakage from related-party pricing to outside holders cannot be sized and the related-party judgment rests on terms and not on amounts.

- The U.S. Petroleum Partners acquisition had not closed in the latest filing, and its funding mix, closing date, inventory payment and any price multiple beyond the earn-out target are not established, so its effect on leverage at ARKO Petroleum is unmeasured.
### Company and operating model
| Area | What the filings show | Credit consequence | Source |

| Business | At 2026-09-30 ARKO operated 1,038 convenience stores, supplied fuel to 2,124 dealer sites and ran 294 cardlock sites in more than 30 states and the District of Columbia; management says it is one of the largest convenience store operators by store count (Management Language). | Site scale and a regional brand portfolio spread local risk, but earnings still rest on fuel and in-store margins in small and mid-sized towns. | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34 |

| Revenue mix | External revenue in nine months 2026: retail 52.17%, wholesale 39.94%, fleet fueling 7.59%; GPMP sells fuel to the other segments at cost plus a fixed margin and is eliminated on consolidation. | Most revenue is fuel resold at thin margins, so revenue size overstates profit and falls with fuel prices; GPMP profit is an intra-group transfer price. | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10 |

| Profit mix | Wholesale, fleet fueling and GPMP, now inside ARKO Petroleum, earned 48.75% of segment operating income in nine months 2026 and 46.25% in FY2025; retail earned the rest. | Nearly half of segment profit now sits in a company with outside holders, so the parent's claim on it runs through dividends. | 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31 |

| Operating model shift | The Transformation Plan converts retail stores to dealer sites supplied by wholesale: stores fell from 1,389 at 2024-12-31 to 1,038 and dealer sites rose from 1,922 to 2,124; conversions added USD 15.6 million of incremental operating income over the twelve months to 2026-09-30 and are expected to be largely complete by the end of 2027. | Less store labor and capital and more fixed-fee fuel supply steady earnings, at the cost of merchandise profit and some site control. | 10-K_2024-12-31_arko_arko-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38 |

| Margin drivers | Merchandise margin was 34.5% in nine months 2026 (33.5% a year earlier) and fuel margin 29.4 cents per gallon (27.0); merchandise revenue fell 12.28% and fuel gallons 7.61% with fewer stores and weak demand. | Margin gains are offsetting volume losses; a further volume fall without margin help would hit coverage. | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42–44 |

| Real estate and leases | At 2025-12-31 ARKO owned 409 properties, including 212 of 1,118 retail stores, and leased 906 retail stores; at 2026-09-30 843 of 1,038 retail stores are leased (81.21%); lease liabilities were USD 1,665.193 million at 2025-12-31 against total debt of USD 912.145 million; operating lease income from dealers rose to USD 52.7 million in 2025. | Fixed lease payments rank alongside debt service in practice, and sublease income grows with dealerization. | 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 139–140 |

| Seasonality and fuel price | Operating income in the second and third quarters is historically well above the first and fourth; in the third quarter of 2026 diesel prices reached record highs and management says sustained high prices could compress margins or raise working capital needs (Management Language). | Liquidity needs peak with fuel prices and in the weaker quarters, which draws on revolvers. | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40 |

| Suppliers and customers | No external customer was more than 10% of revenue; in FY2025 four suppliers each exceeded 10% of purchases (three fuel suppliers at USD 658.815 million, USD 771.508 million and USD 598.361 million, and one merchandise supplier at USD 681.388 million); Core-Mark was the primary wholesale merchandise distributor alongside about 810 direct store delivery distributors, and about 81% of retail fuel locations sold branded fuel. | No customer concentration, but four suppliers carry a large part of purchases, so a supply or terms disruption at one would reach margins quickly. | 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158 |
### Company profile
| Item | Detail | Source |

| Issuer and listing | ARKO Corp., Delaware; common stock listed on Nasdaq as ARKO; accelerated filer; 112,175,416 shares outstanding at 2026-11-03 | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1 |

| Incorporation | Incorporated in Delaware on 2020-08-26 for the business combination of Haymaker Acquisition Corp. II and ARKO Holdings Ltd., an Israeli company | 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6 |
| Headquarters | Richmond, Virginia | 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 1 |

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

Debt at 2026-09-30 carried USD 624.743 million: Senior Notes of USD 347.491 million (USD 350.0 million of principal, due 2029-11-15), the Capital One line at USD 174.431 million (USD 178.1 million drawn, USD 621.4 million unused, due 2028-05-05), M&T debt of USD 98.217 million including a USD 70.2 million term loan and a USD 26.2 million equipment line, and insurance premium notes of USD 4.604 million. The PNC lines had no borrowings and USD 9.0 million of letters of credit outstanding.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60–63

No new bond or loan was issued in 2026; the transactions were an equity offering by a subsidiary, repayment and repurchase of debt, and the refinancing of existing bank loans. On 2026-02-13 ARKO Petroleum completed its initial public offering of 11,111,111 Class A shares at USD 18.00 per share, and on 2026-03-09 it issued 1,459,112 more shares to underwriters, for net proceeds of about USD 206.8 million. ARKO kept 35,000,000 Class B shares, which are 73.6% of the economic interests and 93.3% of the vote, and USD 206.7 million of the proceeds repaid the Capital One line, which an amendment of 2026-01-13 secured with interests in ARKO Petroleum's supply agreements and a pledge of its equity in GPMP.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 21; calculation C40

ARKO repurchased USD 100.0 million of its Senior Notes due 2029 in the nine months to 2026-09-30 for USD 91.858 million, leaving USD 350.0 million outstanding. On 2026-02-11 GPM refinanced and consolidated its M&T real estate loans into a USD 73.0 million term loan due 2031-02-10 and extended an equipment line of up to USD 45.0 million to February 2031. At the listing the PNC line was split into a GPM line and an ARKO Petroleum line, and after the GPM line was raised from USD 56 million to USD 130 million on 2026-08-04 the two lines total USD 214 million; their maturity is the earliest of 2031-02-13 and six months before the maturity of the Senior Notes or the Capital One line.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 60–62

The only announced acquisition is the purchase by ARKO Petroleum of substantially all the assets of U.S. Petroleum Partners, signed on 2026-08-04: about USD 205 million in cash plus the value of inventory, and USD 30 million of ARKO Petroleum stock held in escrow until a true-up that depends on EBITDA targets of USD 31.7 million for the business and USD 2.2 million for certain fuel-related components, with recoupment of up to USD 5.0 million of the cash price possible. The business brings the right to supply fuel to about 400 dealer locations, two fuel terminals and a fleet of more than 50 trucks and trailers; closing is expected later in 2026 and is not certain, and the cash is to be borrowed under existing lines of credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; calculation C35

Two dividends are declared and payable after the balance sheet date: ARKO Petroleum's USD 0.50 per share on 2026-11-30, of which ARKO receives USD 17.5 million on its Class B shares, and ARKO's own USD 0.03 per share on 2026-12-03. These are subsequent events and are not folded into the figures for the nine months.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C49

Overall, ARKO presents medium sponsor and governance risk. The key supported behavior is the repayment of debt with ARKO Petroleum's stock-offering proceeds and the repurchase of notes below par, which matters because it lowers interest cost and raises liquidity and implies lower near-term default risk. Countervailing evidence is the permanent 26.4% outside claim on ARKO Petroleum, payouts above free cash flow and unnamed controlling holders. Further analysis requires the proxy statement, the executed credit documents and the closing terms of the pending acquisition.

## Gaps

- The holders of about 59% of the voting stock are not named and no fund life, pledge or exit intention is stated, because the proxy statement that carries directors, ownership and related-party detail is not supplied; the medium governance rating rests on structure and observed actions. Severity High. Action: obtain the proxy statement.

- Whether ARKO Petroleum and its subsidiaries guarantee the Senior Notes is not stated after the listing, so the notes' direct claim on subsidiary cash flow is not established. Severity High. Action: obtain the indenture and any supplemental indenture.

- Covenant levels, compliance after 2025-12-31 and the capacity for dividends, investments, liens and debt under the PNC, M&T, Capital One and Senior Notes documents are not stated, so legal capacity for shareholder payouts and acquisitions is not measured. Severity High. Action: obtain the credit agreements, the indenture and compliance certificates.

- No amounts are printed for the management services, fuel supply and cost-sharing charges between ARKO and ARKO Petroleum after the listing, so leakage from related-party pricing cannot be sized. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's quarterly report and the proxy statement.

- The closing date, funding mix, inventory payment and pro forma EBITDA of the pending U.S. Petroleum Partners purchase are not stated, so its effect on leverage at ARKO Petroleum is not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the closing announcement and the next quarterly report.

- ARKO Petroleum's own statements, debt and dividend capacity are not supplied, and the parent-only schedule exists only at 2025-12-31, so the parent's upstream cash at 2026-09-30 is not established. Severity Medium. Action: obtain the subsidiary's own reports.

- In the third-quarter report the segment expense tables lose column alignment in the text as supplied, so only segment revenue and operating income were read from them; segment expenses are not analysed. Severity Low. Action: use the aligned tables in the management discussion if segment costs are needed.
- No rating, bond price or loan price is supplied, so no market view of governance risk is stated. Severity Low. Action: obtain rating reports and price sources if wanted.

spans.text: # ARKO Corp. — Fundamental credit
## Request

Issuer: ARKO Corp., issuer id arko-1823794, as of 2026-11-18, credit snapshot pathway. Scope: fundamental credit synthesis of business quality, financial profile, liquidity and refinancing, ownership and financial policy, taken from the five supplied SEC filings and the three earlier handoffs. No rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or portfolio sizing is given.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

ARKO's fundamental credit is adequate: debt to EBITDA fell to 2.75x after a 2026 subsidiary stock offering repaid bank debt, but free cash flow is close to zero, so creditors depend on liquidity and on refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities. Liquidity of about USD 1.0 billion covers the near term, but the only printed maturity schedule predates the 2026 repayments and the unsecured Senior Notes carry a market-based value of 89.23% of principal.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

The strengths are scale, the equity-funded debt reduction and fixed-fee fuel supply; the weaknesses are a 2.74% EBITDA margin, cash interest cover of 3.01x, payouts to shareholders that exceeded free cash flow in 2026 and secured debt of 1.20x EBITDA ranking ahead of the unsecured notes. Financial policy and governance risk are medium.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C10; calculation C20
### Key findings

Leverage is lower because debt fell, not because earnings rose, so the improvement is a one-time step. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 2.75x at 2026-09-30 against 3.85x at 2025-12-31, since total debt fell 31.51% while last-twelve-months reported EBITDA slipped 3.98%. Net debt to EBITDA is 1.94x, which is 1.95x pro forma for the common dividend payable 2026-12-03 and 1.97x pro forma for the subsidiary dividend payable 2026-11-30, each event taken alone, and the effect of the pending acquisition is not established. Counting finance leases lifts total debt to EBITDA to 3.63x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C04; calculation C05; calculation C06; calculation C07; calculation C08

Free cash flow is the weak link and the main reason the profile is adequate rather than strong. Free cash flow was 47.64% of reported EBITDA in FY2024, 27.57% in FY2025 and 0.33% over the last twelve months, and it was negative in the nine months to 2026-09-30, when operating cash flow fell 38.68% while capital spending rose. The swing in receivables, inventory and payables was larger than the whole fall in operating cash flow, so part of the shortfall can reverse as fuel prices settle, but the company also pays dividends and cash interest cover is only 3.01x.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; calculation C32; calculation C31; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59

Margins are thin enough that fuel margin decides earnings. Reported EBITDA is 2.74% of revenue over the last twelve months, and a change of one cent per gallon on 2025 volumes moves gross profit by USD 20.64 million, which is 8.71% of 2025 reported EBITDA. Fixed-fee wholesale supply and dealer conversions dampen this, but the company attributes the 2026 rise in fuel margin to fuel-market volatility, which can reverse, and add-backs are 13.94% of Adjusted EBITDA, so reported EBITDA is the safer measure.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39

Liquidity is adequate for the next year, but the funding calendar from late 2027 is crowded. The company states liquidity of about USD 1.0 billion, including about USD 845 million of undrawn lines whose PNC part depends on a borrowing base. Against that, the Series A preferred redemption right opens on 2027-08-31 for USD 100.0 million, the PNC lines mature on 2027-11-05 on the filing's maturity test unless the Capital One line is extended, and the USD 178.1 million drawn on the Capital One line due 2028-05-05 and the USD 350.0 million of Senior Notes due 2029-11-15 are together 84.53% of total debt.

Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C48; calculation C27; calculation C28; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 61; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147

Noteholders sit behind secured lenders and a partly owned subsidiary. Secured debt of 1.20x EBITDA ranks ahead of the unsecured Senior Notes, which the parent issued and certain domestic subsidiaries guarantee, and after the 2026 offering outside holders own 26.4% of the subsidiary that earned 48.75% of segment operating income, so its dividends reach the parent net of that share. Whether the subsidiary guarantees the notes is not stated, and legal ranking is not assessed here.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20; calculation C40; calculation C39

Market access is open at a price. The Senior Notes were valued at 89.23% of principal at 2026-09-30 against 86.09% at 2025-12-31, each percentage point of extra yield on refinancing USD 350.0 million adds USD 3.50 million a year of interest, and the subsidiary's stock offering shows that equity investors will fund the group's operating businesses. No rating or bond price is supplied, so market access is judged from the company's own fair value estimate.
Basis: calculation C21; calculation C22; calculation C25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 27; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

The business profile is average: large by site count but low in margin, and the Transformation Plan is raising quality at the cost of scale. Retail stores are 25.27% fewer than at the end of 2024 as stores convert to dealer sites or close, merchandise margin rose to 34.5% from 33.5%, and same-store merchandise sales fell only 1.3% in the nine months, with about 90% of that decline from cigarettes, while fuel gallons fell 7.61%.
Basis: calculation C41; calculation C42; Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–48

Fixed lease obligations are a bigger claim on cash flow than debt. Operating and finance lease liabilities were 2.63x total debt at 2026-09-30, operating lease cost in 2025 was 2.21x cash interest, and 81.21% of retail stores are leased, so rent absorbs store profit before debt service does.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C44; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139

Financial policy is moderate. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as medium: no sponsor is named and the 2026 actions favored creditors, but payouts in 2026 exceeded free cash flow, a USD 205 million acquisition is planned at the subsidiary and a Series A claim of USD 100.0 million can be called from 2027-08-31.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147

The primary downside path runs from fuel prices through working capital to revolver borrowing. Sustained record diesel prices and weak demand would lift receivables and inventory, push operating cash flow below capital spending as in 2026, and lead to borrowing on the PNC and Capital One lines to fund payouts and the acquisition. Cash interest cover would reach 2.0x if reported EBITDA fell 33.53% at current interest, an illustrative level because no covenant level is printed.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C26; calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is the speed of the repair. Total debt is 31.51% lower than at the end of 2025, cash interest paid over the last twelve months is 13.38% lower than in 2025, reported cover improved to 3.01x from 2.71x, Adjusted EBITDA grew 8.54% in the nine months, scheduled principal due before 2028 was small on the last printed schedule, and the weak 2026 cash flow comes largely from working capital tied to high fuel prices, which can reverse. Equity investors funded the subsidiary at USD 18.00 per share in 2026, so access to capital is not in doubt today.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C11; calculation C10; calculation C09; calculation C19; calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16

Two developments would move the view toward stronger: free cash flow after payouts turning positive for consecutive quarters, and a Capital One extension that also moves the PNC maturity beyond 2027-11-05, ideally with further Senior Notes repurchased below par without revolver borrowing. Four would move it toward weaker: a second period in which operating cash flow is below capital spending, borrowing under the Capital One line to fund the acquisition without matching EBITDA, a Series A redemption funded from the revolver, or a covenant amendment on terms that are not printed.
Basis: calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21
### Limitations

- The Capital One leverage and interest cover tests and the M&T tests are named but their levels are not printed, so the distance between today's ratios and any breach is not established and liquidity could be tighter than the headline figure suggests.

- The latest maturity schedule is dated 2025-12-31, so the 2028 and 2029 maturities after the 2026 repayments are taken from stated drawn amounts and not from a schedule, which makes the funding calendar approximate until a new schedule is printed.

- No rating, peer metric or bond price is supplied, so the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is qualitative and the market value of the Senior Notes is only the company's own period-end estimate.

- Last-twelve-months figures to 2026-09-30 add unaudited nine-month periods to audited FY2025, so conclusions about the earnings and cash flow trend carry quarter-end timing noise, above all in working capital.
- No management guidance, forecast or standalone ARKO Petroleum statements are supplied, so the outlook is qualitative and the parent's own cash generation after the listing is not established.
### Strengths and weaknesses
Four strengths support the credit and five weaknesses constrain it.

Scale and channel mix give the group shock absorption that most regional operators lack. ARKO had 3,512 sites at 2025-12-31 and revenues of USD 7,643.471 million in FY2025, spread across company-operated stores, dealer supply and fleet fueling, so fixed-fee wholesale profit and fleet fueling profit offset swings in retail fuel margin and support debt service even though group margins are thin.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 30–31; calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C50

Equity-funded debt reduction has cut both leverage and fixed charges. Total debt fell 31.51% and last-twelve-months cash interest paid is 13.38% lower than in 2025, because stock-offering proceeds repaid bank debt and Senior Notes were bought back below par, which lowers default risk and lifts cash interest cover to 3.01x.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04; calculation C11; calculation C10

Liquidity of about USD 1.0 billion is the main protection for creditors. It includes undrawn committed lines of USD 845.2 million before any PNC borrowing-base limit, against scheduled principal that was small before 2028 on the last printed schedule, so near-term debt service and the acquisition cash can be met without capital markets.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C49; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

Fixed-fee supply and dealer conversions make part of the earnings less volatile. Wholesale fuel supply locations earned 6.3 cents per gallon on fixed fees in 2025 and the group-set margin for the fuel-supply segment is 6.0 cents per gallon in 2026, while site operating expenses fell 6.83% in the nine months, which improves margin stability at the cost of merchandise profit.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 72; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41

Thin margins make earnings highly sensitive to fuel margin. Reported EBITDA is 2.74% of revenue and one cent per gallon on 2025 volumes is USD 20.64 million, or 8.71% of 2025 reported EBITDA, so a small compression in fuel margin or a loss of gallons moves cover and leverage quickly.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C12; calculation C23; calculation C24

Free cash flow is close to zero, which leaves payouts and debt service dependent on balances and borrowings. Free cash flow was 0.33% of reported EBITDA over the last twelve months against 47.64% in FY2024, and add-backs are 13.94% of Adjusted EBITDA, so deleveraging after the equity proceeds depends on a recovery in working capital and margin.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C17; calculation C15; calculation C18

The funding calendar from late 2027 is crowded. The Series A redemption right of USD 100.0 million opens on 2027-08-31, the PNC lines mature on 2027-11-05 on the stated test unless the Capital One line is extended, and the Capital One and Senior Notes maturities of 2028 and 2029 are 84.53% of total debt, so refinancing capacity matters more than current liquidity.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C48; calculation C28; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147

Secured debt and a minority interest rank ahead of the unsecured notes. Secured debt is 1.20x EBITDA, outside holders own 26.4% of the subsidiary that earned 48.75% of segment operating income, and the guarantor scope of the notes after the listing is not stated, so the notes' claim runs through the parent and dividends that reach it net of the outside share.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C20; calculation C40; calculation C39

Fixed lease obligations and falling volumes erode flexibility. Lease liabilities are 2.63x total debt, operating lease cost is 2.21x cash interest, and fuel gallons fell 7.61% in the nine months with 25.27% fewer retail stores, so a downturn meets large fixed charges.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C33; calculation C34; calculation C42; calculation C41
