### Credit-relevant company description

ARKO is a convenience store operator and fuel wholesaler whose profit comes from fuel margins and in-store merchandise margins on a very large, low-margin revenue base. At 2026-09-30 it operated 1,038 stores, supplied fuel to 2,124 dealer sites and ran 294 cardlock sites in more than 30 states; retail supplied 52.17% of nine-month external revenue, wholesale 39.94% and fleet fueling 7.59%, and fuel was 83.08% of revenues, so revenue size says little about profit. Wholesale sells on fixed fees per gallon and management describes fleet fueling as a durable cash flow business, so both give more predictable cash flow than retail, where margins move with wholesale fuel costs and local competition, and operating income is seasonal, with the second and third quarters well above the first and fourth.

Basis: calculation C51; calculation C52; calculation C50; calculation C37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9

The model is being reshaped by the Transformation Plan, which converts retail stores to dealer sites supplied by wholesale, and by 26 acquisitions since 2013, none of them in 2025 or the nine months of 2026. For creditors this lowers store labor and capital but also merchandise profit, adds fixed-fee supply and rent, and leaves cash-flow visibility better in the contracted channels than in retail; debt service capacity rests on reported EBITDA of USD 227.442 million over the last twelve months, and refinancing confidence rests on that earnings base and on liquidity rather than on any sponsor.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 37–38
### Ownership and group structure

ARKO is a public company with no sponsor named in its filings: a limited group of unnamed stockholders held about 59% of the vote at 2025-12-31, down from about 67%, and the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer leads both ARKO and its listed subsidiary. Business & governance rates sponsor and governance risk as medium: the 2026 actions reduced debt and cost creditors only the 26.4% outside share of the subsidiary's dividends, but payouts exceeded free cash flow in 2026, agreements between ARKO and the subsidiary were set without a separate board, and a Series A preferred claim of USD 100.0 million can be called from 2027-08-31.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C45; calculation C40

The group has three debt levels: Senior Notes at the parent, guaranteed by certain domestic subsidiaries; the Capital One line at GPMP inside ARKO Petroleum, secured by pledges over the subsidiary's supply agreements and its equity in GPMP; and the PNC and M&T facilities at GPM and at ARKO Petroleum. ARKO holds 73.6% of the subsidiary's economics and 93.3% of its vote, the parent's own cash was USD 2.577 million at 2025-12-31, and parent-only statements show that note service depends on interest and repayments from subsidiaries, so the dividend limits in the Capital One and PNC documents are the link between operating cash flow and the notes. Covenant capacity is not assessed here.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 159–160; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is mostly pass-through fuel, so it is cyclical and price-driven: revenues grew 11.28% in the nine months to 2026-09-30 although fuel gallons fell 7.61%, because the average price of fuel rose, and merchandise revenue fell 12.28% as stores closed or converted and same-store sales declined. Retail fuel margin is the swing factor because retail prices lag wholesale costs; the company says margins are lower when costs rise gradually and higher when costs fall or are volatile. Wholesale and consignment contracts earn a fixed fee or share gross profit, which largely removes exposure to commodity price movements in the wholesale channel.

Basis: calculation C38; calculation C42; calculation C53; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 41–44; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9

Demand is discretionary at the margin and shrinking in volume: same-store fuel gallons fell about 5% to 6% in every period, same-store merchandise sales fell 1.3% in the nine months with about 90% of the decline from cigarettes, and no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but four suppliers each exceed 10% of purchases. Loyalty enrollment of about 2.7 million, up 11.2% from a year earlier, and fixed-fee dealer contracts give some stickiness, yet retail revenue is not contracted. Revenue is therefore large, volatile in price terms and declining in volume.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–48; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 70; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Costs are largely fixed once stores are open: site operating expenses were 6.83% lower in the nine months because stores were closed or converted, general and administrative expenses rose 1.72%, and rent is a large fixed element, with operating lease cost of USD 192.929 million inside site operating expenses in 2025. Fuel and merchandise costs pass through to prices with a lag, so margins are exposed to input-cost swings, and store wages are a continuing pressure with about 8,450 store employees at the end of 2025.

Basis: calculation C35; calculation C36; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 139; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 39

Margins can be defended under moderate volume pressure because conversions cut store costs and wholesale fees are fixed, but not against a sharp compression in fuel margin: one cent per gallon on 2025 volumes is USD 20.64 million, 8.71% of reported EBITDA, and the reported EBITDA margin is only 2.74%. Operating deleverage is the main risk, because rent, labor and depreciation stay while gallons fall.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C12
### Capital intensity and free cash flow conversion

Capital intensity is modest, with purchases of property and equipment at 1.62% of revenue over the last twelve months, but conversion of EBITDA to free cash flow has collapsed: 47.64% in FY2024, 27.57% in FY2025 and 0.33% over the last twelve months. Cash interest paid is USD 75.590 million, cash taxes were USD 6.188 million in the nine months to 2026-09-30, and 2025 cash taxes were lowered by a timing benefit of USD 26.9 million from the 2025 tax law change, so the 2025 free cash flow of USD 65.299 million flatters the underlying level.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C13; calculation C15; calculation C16; calculation C17; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 142; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 9

Working capital absorbed cash in 2026: receivables rose USD 101.894 million and inventory USD 31.938 million against a USD 56.209 million rise in payables, and lower dealer deposits cut cash by about USD 14.9 million. Capital spending of USD 104.945 million in the nine months includes fee properties, new-to-industry stores, fleet fueling sites, remodels and EV chargers, much of it discretionary growth spending that could be cut, although the split between maintenance and growth capital is not stated. EBITDA therefore does not currently convert to free cash flow for deleveraging; equity proceeds and liquidity have done that work.
Basis: calculation C29; calculation C31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 59
### Competitive forces in credit terms

Rivalry is intense and limits margin durability: the annual report names 7-Eleven and Speedway, Circle K, Casey's, Murphy USA, QuikTrip, Royal Farms, Sheetz and Wawa as large competitors, many building new sites in ARKO's markets, and says competitors often sell unbranded fuel at lower prices, so retail fuel and merchandise margins have little protection.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14–15

The threat of new entrants is moderate: the barriers are the financial strength needed for fuel supply agreements and the capital for sites, but national chains are building new-to-industry sites and ARKO's own plan to open such sites needs the same capital.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 14–16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 36

Substitutes are a slow-moving risk: ARKO's 295 electric vehicle chargers at 100 locations at 2026-09-30, up from 211 at 72 at 2025-12-31, are small, while dollar stores, pharmacies and grocery and warehouse fuel sites compete for snacks, beer and fuel, which pressures merchandise and volume.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15

Buyer power is low in each channel because no customer exceeds 10% of revenue, but retail customers are price-sensitive and dealers can change suppliers at renewal, so wholesale margins depend on competitive pricing inside fixed-fee frameworks.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 15; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 158

Supplier power is the stronger force: four suppliers each exceeded 10% of purchases in 2025, three for fuel and one for merchandise, Core-Mark is the primary wholesale merchandise distributor, and fuel supply contracts run to various dates through 2032, so supply terms and rebates set margins and a disruption would reach liquidity through inventory financing.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 136
### Macro, regulatory and political factors

Only two groups of factors change the credit conclusion. Economic and political factors matter because fuel prices were volatile in 2026 with the Middle East conflict and supply disruptions, diesel reached record highs in the third quarter, and management says sustained high diesel prices or supply constraints could reduce gallons, compress margins or raise working capital needs, which is the main path from macro conditions to liquidity; 44.0% of debt bore variable rates at 2026-09-30, so a one percentage point rise would add about USD 2.8 million of annual debt service. Regulatory factors matter because cigarette sales explain about 90% of the same-store merchandise decline, tobacco consumption and regulation are named risks, and environmental rules on underground tanks require remediation spending, with environmental capital expenditure of about USD 3.3 million in 2025. Social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver on the provided materials.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 64; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 17
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths: scale and channel mix across retail, dealer and fleet sites; equity-funded debt reduction with lower cash interest; liquidity of about USD 1.0 billion; fixed-fee wholesale supply and dealer conversions.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58

Weaknesses: thin margins with high sensitivity to fuel margin; near-zero free cash flow; secured debt and a minority interest ahead of the unsecured notes; fixed lease obligations and falling volumes.

Opportunities: completing dealer conversions by the end of 2027, new fleet fueling and new-to-industry sites, extending the Capital One and PNC facilities, further Senior Notes repurchases below par, and the U.S. Petroleum Partners acquisition if it closes with limited debt.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 36–37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39–40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position are average: ARKO is large by site count and revenue but regional, and the filings give no peer metrics. Competitive advantage is weak to average, because regional brands, loyalty enrollment and site locations are the only differentiators and suppliers set key terms. Business diversification is average: fuel supply, merchandise and fleet fueling balance one another, but four suppliers carry a large part of purchases. Cost and capex flexibility is average: growth capital can be cut, but rent, labor and depreciation are fixed.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; calculation C13

Margin stability is weak: the reported EBITDA margin is 2.74% and one cent per gallon is 8.71% of EBITDA, although fixed-fee supply and conversions are improving it. Free cash flow stability is weak: conversion fell from 47.64% in FY2024 to 0.33% over the last twelve months, helped in 2025 by a tax timing benefit. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average: equity investors funded the subsidiary and the Senior Notes are valued at 89.23% of principal, but there is no rating or sponsor and the funding calendar is crowded from late 2027. Liquidity position is average on a stated USD 1.0 billion with a PNC borrowing-base limit and no printed covenant levels. Financial policy and governance is average, in line with the medium risk rating for sponsor and governance.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12; calculation C24; calculation C15; calculation C17; calculation C21

The main credit supports are liquidity, lower leverage and the fixed-fee channels; the constraints are thin cash generation, claims ahead of the notes and the 2027 to 2029 calendar. The trend is improving on leverage and weakening on cash conversion. Key missing datapoints are covenant levels, a current maturity schedule, the guarantor list, standalone statements for the subsidiary, any rating and peer metrics.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over 12 to 24 months the tailwinds are lower cash interest after the 2026 repayments, dealer conversions adding fixed-fee income that management puts at USD 15.6 million over twelve months, a higher merchandise margin and the chance to extend the Capital One and PNC facilities. The headwinds are volume decline, fuel-price volatility that raises working capital, tax on subsidiary dividends, the pending acquisition's borrowings, the Series A redemption right from 2027-08-31 and the PNC maturity of 2027-11-05; together they make 2027 the test of whether free cash flow has recovered.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11; calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 45; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147

Over three to five years the question is whether the shift to dealers and fleet fueling lifts earnings quality enough to refinance USD 528.1 million of 2028 and 2029 maturities at an acceptable cost: the Senior Notes are valued below par, so each percentage point of extra yield on USD 350.0 million adds USD 3.50 million a year of interest, while structural headwinds are falling gallons, cigarette decline and electric vehicle adoption. No management guidance is supplied, so the outlook is qualitative.
Basis: calculation C27; calculation C25; calculation C21; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a sustained spike in wholesale fuel prices, with diesel at record highs as in the third quarter of 2026, together with weaker demand. The first operational break is working capital: receivables and inventory rise as they did in 2026, when three working-capital lines absorbed more cash than the whole fall in operating cash flow, and retail fuel margin is squeezed when costs rise gradually. Operating cash flow then stays below capital spending, so free cash flow turns negative and the payouts to shareholders and the dividends to outside holders of the subsidiary are met from cash balances and revolver borrowing.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C31; calculation C32; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 39; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9

Financially, borrowing on the Capital One and PNC lines raises debt while EBITDA falls; reported cash interest cover would be 2.0x if EBITDA fell 33.53% at current interest, an illustrative level because no covenant level is printed, and a PNC borrowing base shrinks if receivables and inventory fall. The leverage and refinancing consequence is that the 2027 calendar of the Series A redemption right and the PNC maturity of 2027-11-05 arrives with less free cash flow, and the USD 205 million acquisition, if borrowed, would add debt first and earnings later. Management levers are cutting growth capital, stopping buybacks and dividends, slowing conversions and drawing the Capital One line, whose unused amount was USD 621.4 million. Resilience appears sufficient to avoid liquidity distress within 12 to 24 months on stated liquidity, but refinancing risk in 2028 and 2029 would rise sharply.

Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C26; calculation C48; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_arko_arko-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 18–21; 10-K_2025-12-31_arko_arko-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 147
### Overall credit view

Overall, ARKO presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, a fixed-fee wholesale channel, a fleet fueling base and a repaired balance sheet, but credit quality is constrained by thin margins, near-zero free cash flow, secured debt and a minority interest ahead of the unsecured notes, and a crowded funding calendar from late 2027. Cash-flow durability appears weak to adequate because free cash flow conversion fell to 0.33% of EBITDA while 81.21% of retail stores are leased. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on extending the Capital One line before 2027-11-05, on the fuel market, which drives working capital and margin, and on whether the subsidiary's dividends keep reaching the parent. The primary downside path is a fuel price spike that turns working capital into revolver borrowing ahead of the 2027 to 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require covenant levels, a current maturity schedule, the guarantor list and standalone statements for the subsidiary. Fundamental credit completed. Top risk: refinancing the 2027 to 2029 obligations from thin free cash flow.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C17; calculation C44; calculation C48
